brandEssence: Warm, confident and botanical: a matte sage bottle with quiet cream lettering, shown in strong natural sun against rich, earthy colour, natural stone and white cotton.

palette.name: VERDA Sage
palette.usage: Primary brand colour; bottle body. Use as the dominant colour in brand graphics and as a background block behind cream text.

palette.name: Shadow Sage
palette.usage: Shaded side of the bottle; use for depth, secondary panels or darker text on light grounds. Do not replace the primary sage with it.

palette.name: Label Cream
palette.usage: All text set on sage (wordmark, product name, back copy); also the barcode sticker ground. Never pure white on sage.

palette.name: Cap White
palette.usage: Flip-top cap and packshot background (seamless off-white). Use for clean negative space.

palette.name: Travertine
palette.usage: Lifestyle surfaces and tiles; warm neutral backgrounds and secondary layout fills.

palette.name: Terracotta
palette.usage: Small accent only (the plant pot in lifestyle). Keep under ~5% of any frame or layout.

display.description: The VERDA wordmark: light-weight classical serif, all caps, very wide letter-spacing, cream on sage, centred horizontally on the bottle front.
display.googleFontMatch: Cormorant Garamond (Medium) – approximate; use the supplied wordmark artwork wherever possible
rules: Wordmark is always set in ALL CAPS: VERDA.
Letter-spacing roughly 0.2–0.3em; letters must never touch or appear crowded.
Wordmark is centred horizontally and sits above the product name with a clear gap (approx. 1.5–2x the cap height).
The wordmark is the largest text element; product name is approx. 40% of its cap height or smaller.
Do not set the wordmark in bold, italic, outline, drop shadow or gradient.
Do not use the serif for product names, body copy or instructions.

body.description: Clean geometric sans serif in a regular/book weight, used for product name, descriptor line and back-of-pack copy. Cream on sage.
rules: Product name in Title Case on two centred lines, e.g. 'Daily Hydrating' / 'Shampoo'.
Descriptor line is small, lowercase and centred near the base: 'with aloe & oat · 400 mL / 13.5 fl oz'; use a middle dot (·) between items and a slash between metric and imperial; metric first.
Use '&' rather than 'and' in short descriptor lines.
Back-of-pack copy is left-aligned in a single narrow column; subheads are medium weight, sentence case, ending in a colon ('How to use:', 'Ingredients:').
Ingredients are listed in INCI form, comma-separated, ending with a full stop.
Body text stays in one weight plus medium for subheads; no bold blocks, no all-caps body copy.

lighting: Lifestyle and In-use: hard, warm, low-angle natural sun from a window on the left, golden-hour tone, with shaped shadows such as window-pane bars or leaf shadows.
Packshots: soft, even, diffused studio light; no hard specular hotspots; a gentle vertical tonal falloff across the matte bottle.
Packshots: a faint soft contact shadow directly beneath the bottle only.
Lifestyle and In-use: shadows fall to the right, with a clear difference between lit and shadowed areas; highlights warm, never blown out on the label.
settings: Packshots: plain off-white seamless background (#F6F6F4), no environment.
Lifestyle: a bathroom with a window, a richly coloured wall and a stone ledge or countertop.
The wall stays soft (shallow depth of field) but keeps its full colour.
In-use: a sunlit bathroom with soft steam and a wet stone ledge. A dry bathroom suits a hair mask or scalp treatment, and a hotel bathroom counter suits a travel set.
materials: Bottle: matte, soft-touch sage finish with no gloss; label printed directly onto the bottle (no paper label) except the cream barcode sticker on the back.
Cap: white, matte flip-top with a thumb notch facing front.
Surfaces: travertine or limestone with visible natural pitting; walls of zellige tile, limewash or tadelakt plaster.
props: Live aloe vera plant in a plain terracotta pot (ties to 'with aloe' on pack).
Neatly folded white terry towels, stacked.
Water droplets on the bottle and cap are permitted in bathroom scenes.
Maximum two or three props per frame; nothing branded other than VERDA.
In-use: the action is the subject, so use one prop at most. Leave out the aloe plant and stacked towels.
composition: Packshots: single bottle, upright, dead-centre, straight-on at label height, full bottle in frame with generous even margin (bottle approx. 80–85% of frame height).
Front packshot shows wordmark and product name fully legible; back packshot shows full instructions, ingredients and barcode.
Lifestyle: bottle is the hero, standing upright, slightly left of centre, front label facing camera, filling roughly half the frame height.

Lifestyle: camera level with the ledge, at about mid-bottle height, with only a sliver of the ledge's top visible, so the straight-on bottle sits naturally; props behind and to the right, lower than the bottle's shoulder.
Square (1:1) framing as the default format.
Label text in any generated image must exactly match that product's real pack: check spelling and spacing before approval.

In-use: a person's hands or hair mid-use in the right two thirds, with no face. The bottle stands separately on the open ledge at left, at about half the frame height or less, and is never held or overlapped.
avoid: Glossy, transparent or metallic bottle finishes, or any shift from the sage colour.
Garbled, misspelled or unevenly spaced label text (e.g. 'fl ez', split wordmark).
Pump or screw caps, or a cap colour other than white.
Cool/blue or harsh flash lighting, coloured gels, dramatic black backgrounds.
Busy clutter, multiple competing products, or other brands' packaging.
Plastic or artificial plants, neon or synthetic-looking props, glitter or splash effects.
Tilted, floating or lying-down bottles in packshots.
Flat, pale beige-on-beige scenes, even light with no shadow shapes, and a washed-out look.
backdrops: Glazed terracotta zellige tile with crisp window-pane shadows.
Ochre limewash plaster with palm-leaf shadows.
Deep olive tadelakt plaster cut by one warm shaft of sun.
Burnt sienna clay plaster with a hard-edged stripe of sun.

textOnImage: Set headlines in the sans (Jost) in Title Case or sentence case; reserve the wide-tracked serif caps solely for the VERDA name.
On sage or dark areas use Label Cream (#F1EDDF); on light/travertine areas use Shadow Sage (#7D9073). Never pure black or pure white text.
Centre-align short headline text, left-align any multi-line body text, mirroring front and back of pack.
Place text over calm, out-of-focus areas (wall tile, background) and never over the bottle label.
Keep overlays to one headline plus at most one short supporting line; small supporting lines may use the '·' separator style.
No text boxes with heavy fills, outlines, drop shadows or effects; use generous margins (at least 6% of frame width).

traits: Concise and plain: instructions in short imperative phrases ('Massage into wet hair, rinse.').
Descriptive rather than promotional: name the product by what it is ('Daily Hydrating Shampoo').
Ingredient-forward: reference only on-pack ingredients such as aloe and oat.
Quiet, lowercase-friendly details for secondary lines.
Precise with facts: exact volumes in mL and fl oz.
avoid: Claims, benefits or results not stated on the pack.
Exclamation marks, superlatives and hype words.
ALL CAPS copy other than the VERDA wordmark.
Invented brand history, values, certifications or origin stories.
Long paragraphs or jargon beyond the INCI ingredient list.
